milestone.name: signed annotated tag becomes provider-verified release anchor
milestone.revision: A provider-verified annotated tag is a stronger release anchor than mutable release metadata: exact tag object 2f3a... is signed/verified and names exact target commit 11926..., while the live release object itself reported immutable=false. Scheduled Chat can consume the signed-tag -> target -> file identity chain without local cryptographic execution, but only under explicit GitHub-provider trust and only for preexisting evidence.

negative_evidence: A GitHub release page/object is not necessarily immutable; live v3.1.3 release metadata reported immutable=false.
A signed annotated tag authenticates the tag object's target under provider trust, not the semantic correctness of target files.
Raw signature bytes were not treated as proof.

frontier.action: Apply a bounded text parser to a small readable file at the verified tag target, preserving separate steps: signed tag admission -> exact target/file identity -> parsed semantic predicate.
Find/test a lightweight tag and require signed-tag origin rejection, while permitting an independently provider-verified target commit to be classified under the weaker commit origin if exact.
Generalize origin choice: signed tag for release-intent/name binding, signed commit for source-state binding, own repo identity for role-local state.
